title: Avoir raison, faire confiance, faire partie
summary: Use common `avoir` and `faire` expressions without translating English be or make word for word.
objectives: Express being right, wrong, lucky or ashamed with `avoir`.
Use `faire` expressions for intention, pain, fear, trust, belonging and waiting in line.

sources.label: Public A2 index: topic-coverage reference only

sections.title: Keep the French verb inside the expression
paragraphs: Use `avoir raison/tort` to be right/wrong and `avoir de la chance` to be lucky. `Avoir honte de` means be ashamed of something or of doing something. The noun `la honte` (f.) means shame. English be does not decide the French verb.

`Faire exprès de` + infinitive means deliberately do something. After a negative sentence, `je ne l'ai pas fait exprès` means I did not do it on purpose. It denies intention, not necessarily the event itself.
points: Present `avoir`: `j'ai, tu as, il/elle/on a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont`. `Passé composé`: `j'ai eu ... elles ont eu`. Present `faire`: `je fais, tu fais, il/elle/on fait, nous faisons, vous faites, ils/elles font`. `Passé composé`: `j'ai fait ... elles ont fait`.
Do not change the fixed noun because the subject is plural: `nous avons raison`, `elles ont honte`.

examples.french: Tu **as raison** ; j'**ai tort** sur ce point.
examples.english: You are right; I am wrong on this point.

examples.french: Nous **avons eu de la chance** avec la météo.
examples.english: We were lucky with the weather.
He is ashamed of his mistake.

examples.french: Je **n'ai pas fait exprès de** te réveiller.
examples.english: I did not wake you up on purpose.
examples.note: The waking happened; intention is denied.

sections.title: The effect and the person affected
paragraphs: `Faire mal à` can describe physical pain: `le dos me fait mal`. `Faire du mal à` means cause harm, which may be physical, emotional or more general. Their meanings can overlap; do not invent a rule that `du mal` is only emotional. `Faire peur à` means frighten someone; the frightening thing is the subject, and the affected person can be `me/te/lui/nous/vous/leur`.

`Faire confiance à` means trust someone; `faire partie de` means be part of a group. Keep `à` with `confiance` and `de` with `partie`. `Faire la queue` means wait in line; `faire la file` is also familiar in Canadian French. These are fixed expressions, not literal instructions to make an object.
points: `La queue` (f.) means a line of people in this expression. `Faire partie` uses `partie` with final `e`, not `parti` (a political party or a participle).

examples.french: Cette chaussure **me fait mal** ; je ne veux pas **faire du mal à** mon pied.
examples.english: This shoe hurts me; I do not want to harm my foot.
examples.note: Pain and possible damage can both be physical.

examples.french: Je **fais confiance à** cette équipe et je **fais partie du** groupe.
examples.english: I trust this team and I am part of the group.

examples.french: Nous **faisons la queue** pour acheter les billets.
examples.english: We are waiting in line to buy tickets.
examples.note: The expression names waiting, not an act of making.

mistakes.avoid: Je fais confiance de mon médecin.
mistakes.prefer: Je fais confiance à mon médecin.

sections.title: Retain the expression when replacing its complement
paragraphs: With `avoir honte de` a person, a stressed pronoun follows `de`: `de moi, de toi, de lui/d'elle, de nous, de vous, d'eux/d'elles`. With an infinitive, `de` introduces what causes the shame. With `faire confiance à`, a recipient pronoun goes before the relevant verb or auxiliary instead: `lui faire confiance`, `lui avoir fait confiance`.
Negative ordinary luck uses `je n'ai pas de chance`, whereas the positive expression has `de la chance`. The negative changes the partitive quantity, not the noun's feminine gender.
points: Choose the complete expression before deciding whether a pronoun follows a preposition or precedes a verb.

examples.french: Elle a **honte d'eux**, mais elle n'a pas honte **de leur parler**.
examples.english: She is ashamed of them, but she is not ashamed of speaking to them.
examples.note: A stressed pronoun after `de` contrasts with an infinitive construction.

examples.french: Nous **lui avons fait confiance** pour la livraison.
examples.english: We trusted him or her with the delivery.
examples.note: The indirect pronoun precedes the auxiliary.

examples.french: Ils **n'ont pas eu de chance** avec les horaires.
examples.english: They were unlucky with the schedules.

practice.prompt: Use avoir in the present: Vous ___ raison.
Supply the missing article phrase: Elle a ___ chance.
practice.explanation: The expression is avoir de la chance.

practice.prompt: Supply à or de: Nous faisons partie ___ cette association.
Supply faire in the present: Ils ___ la queue.
Use avoir tort in the present: Je ___ sur la date.
Supply de or à: Nous avons honte ___ cette erreur.
Supply the fixed adverb meaning on purpose: Elle a fait ___ de passer plus tôt.
Use faire in the present: Les genoux me ___ mal.
practice.explanation: The knees are the plural subject.

practice.prompt: Complete the expression meaning cause harm: Cette rumeur lui fait ___ mal.
practice.explanation: Faire du mal means harm, here emotional or reputational.

practice.prompt: Replace à mes enfants: Le tonnerre ___ fait peur.
practice.explanation: The affected people are indirect objects.

practice.prompt: Supply à or de: Tu fais confiance ___ ta voisine.
Supply the fixed noun meaning line: Vous faites la ___ devant le cinéma.
practice.explanation: Faire la queue is widespread; faire la file is also accepted, notably in Canada.

practice.prompt: Use avoir in the passé composé: Nous ___ de la chance.
practice.explanation: Avoir has eu after the auxiliary.

practice.prompt: Contract de + le: Elle fait partie ___ comité.
Faire du mal can refer to:
choices: Physical harm as well as emotional or other harm.
Only emotional harm, never physical harm.
answers: Physical harm as well as emotional or other harm.
practice.explanation: The expression is not restricted to emotional injury.

practice.prompt: Je ne l'ai pas fait exprès denies primarily:
choices: That the event happened at all.
practice.explanation: The speaker may acknowledge the event while denying doing it deliberately.

practice.prompt: Replace de ses voisines with a stressed pronoun: Il a honte de ses voisines.
practice.explanation: De remains and elides before elles.

practice.prompt: Replace à la médiatrice with lui: J'ai fait confiance à la médiatrice.
practice.explanation: Lui comes before ai, not after the participle.

practice.prompt: Make this sentence negative with ne ... pas: Tu as eu de la chance.
answers: Tu n'as pas eu de chance.
practice.explanation: The negative surrounds as and changes ordinary partitive de la to de.

production_task.prompt: Write a calm apology after accidentally interrupting a community meeting. Acknowledge the mistake and reassure the organiser.
production_task.model_answer: Vous avez raison : j'ai interrompu la discussion. Je ne l'ai pas fait exprès. J'ai honte de cette erreur et je ferai plus attention. Je fais confiance à votre équipe et je suis heureux de faire partie du groupe.
production_task.translation: You are right: I interrupted the discussion. I did not do it on purpose. I am ashamed of this mistake and I will be more careful. I trust your team and I am happy to be part of the group.
rubric: Distinguish denying intent from denying the event.
